body: Hi, thanks for reporting. Are you referring to the output in the stacktrace?
Yes. it is part of the stack trace
but I don't think its the Stack Trace's fault.

Thanks for reporting the issue. In the future could you report any security issues using the security [at] cakephp.org mailing list?  Thankfully this is issue is only present in development deployments as stack traces are disabled in production deployments.
Well I've met it in some prodution site. Is it possible?

Of course it is possible to deploy an application in development mode to a production server. Exposing stack traces at all in a production setting is a bad idea, not to mention the other inefficient or bad things that can occur when an app is incorrectly deployed.

In any case, I'll get this fixed.

Bottom line here - to make things clear:
Debug mode needs to be 0 for productive websites. So this is not a security issue and especially no exploit.
It can only be happening in the development process - by the developers themselves then.

For accidental debug deployments or alike it is sure good to cover this edge case as well, though :)

Thanks. 
Do you mind if I take credit on it as an exploit?
Like submiting it to Exploit DB or others after you'll fix it?

Did you not read my previous message?
I just stated that this is no exploit. It is your own fault if you deploy with debug mode > 0. You should never do that.
Failing do turn debug features off when deploying is irresponsible and besides other issues will lead to these things. Not only for CakePHP but any PHP for that matter.

So bottom line: You do not need to submit it to Exploit DB or any other site.
This issue can be easily treated and solved as a bugfix for the development process - and does not effect any productive CakePHP site. Very important! In case some people only read the headline of this issue.

Tip for staging servers/URLs: Hide them behind htaccess password protection for example. No one except developers and internal testers should ever have access to this potentially debug-mode-on site.

Ok 
Thanks anyway

@IdoNaor1337 I'm having some issues reproducing the issue. I inferred that from your paste `[SomeString]` needed to be a valid controller name, and that the issue is with the stack trace shown on the "Missing method" error page,  but the provided string does not produce an alert on my machine using Firefox 22 on OSX. When I view the page source all the quotes around the and angle brackets are correctly HTML escaped or URL encoded.
I tested using Apache2.2 and PHP 5.3.6 using mod_php with the DocumentRoot set to app/webroot.
try 'Users'
Here is what I tried using curl https://gist.github.com/markstory/7310226. All the XSS occurrences are properly quoted.

I tried reproducing this on another machine and was unable to. I tried with both the `master` branch and the current `2.4.2` tag. Since we can't confirm this issue, I'm going to close it until a more consistent way to reproduce the issue  comes up. If you'd like to send it by email you can send it to security[at]cakephp.org

Anyone noticed that in order to get this type of code highlighting output: ``` html         $response = $this->_invoke($controller, $request, $response); ``` `highlight_string()` must be called with a string that doesn't contain an opening PHP tag? Looking at the code this was the case up to [CakePHP 2.2.4](https://github.com/cakephp/cakephp/blob/2.2.4/lib/Cake/Utility/Debugger.php#L427), [after that](https://github.com/cakephp/cakephp/blob/2.2.5/lib/Cake/Utility/Debugger.php#L429) CakePHP prepends `
The leading `<?php` was prepended in 1e49be3472b27fd7b67094eaab78cae84db3d893 The opening `<?php` will be present if the excerpt includes the first line of the file.

Not sure whether this was just ment as additional info, or you were trying to answer my "question"? I can see how it works, and that's why I wondering about the output the OP posted, because AFAICT, in later CakePHP versions this would only be possible in case `strpos` or `highlight_string` wouldn't work as expected, ie either `strpos` would need to not return `false` for a needle that doesn't exist, or `highlight_string` would need to ignore the opening PHP tag.

In a nutshell, I was just wondering if the OP maybe stumbled over a PHP bug (regardless of whether there is a problem with the CakePHP code or not).
Maybe OP posted a 2.2.4 bug and mixed up the numbers. Also, his line number is off by one in the latest release...
